hypotheses.justification: The statement does not use DecidableEq V. `G.dist`, `MooreHyp G` (needs only `[Fintype V]` and `[DecidableRel G.Adj]`), `G.Coloring Bool`, `G.Adj` and `a ≠ b` all elaborate without it. The proof uses it only indirectly, because `pred_unique` has an `[DecidableEq V]` argument, and the other lemmas it calls may also take one from the `variable` line. Without the variable, put `classical` at the start of the proof, and every such instance argument is then filled by `Classical.propDecidable`. The conclusion is a Prop about `dist` and does not depend on the chosen decidability instance. The theorem stays true and provable. I did not report `col`: it looks derivable from `H` mathematically, but nothing in the library does that. I did not report `haw`, `hbw` or `hab` either. If `a = w`, then `b` can have distance 6 (the other neighbour of `l` is the distance-4 predecessor), and the conclusion fails. If `a = b`, the conclusion is contradictory.
